xref.title: Chicago River Raw Sewage Incident – August 8, 2004, Kinzie Street Bridge, 800 lbs of Waste onto Tourist Boat
xref.body: At 1:18 pm on August 8, 2004, a Dave Matthews Band tour bus driven by Stephen Wooll crossed the Kinzie Street Bridge in Chicago — a metal grate structure over the Chicago River. Wooll took the opportunity to empty the bus's septic system through the grate. Directly beneath the bridge at that moment was the sightseeing boat *Little Lady*, loaded with approximately 100 tourists looking up at the Chicago skyline. Security cameras on the bridge captured the entire incident. Wooll was sentenced to 18 months probation, 150 hours of community service, and fined $10,000; a $70,000 lawsuit followed for violation of environmental laws. Dave Matthews and the band cooperated fully with the investigation, offering DNA samples to positively identify the waste, and donated $50,000 to Friends of the Chicago River. "800 pounds of human waste... there was a sightseeing boat called the Little Lady."

xref.title: Admiration from Renowned Artists
xref.body: O'Hara garnered significant praise and admiration from many influential musicians; Morrissey requested her for vocalizations on his single "November Spawned a Demon," and Michael Stipe of R.E.M., Radiohead, Bruce Cockburn, Dave Matthews, and Nick Cave were all noted fans of her distinct music. "Moresy was such a fan that he asked her to do some vocalizations on his single November Spawn Demonstrer. Michael Steip couldn't get enough of her. Radiohead, Bruce Coburn, Dave Matthews, Nick Cave, they were all fans."

xref.title: Long-term KISS Roadie and Wig Specialist
xref.body: Dave Matthews worked for KISS for 30 years, primarily responsible for looking after the band's wigs. His duties included responding to emergencies, such as dousing Gene Simmons with a wet towel when the hairspray on his wig caught fire. "There was a guy named Dave Matthews who worked for KISS for 30 years. And his main job was to look after the band's wigs."

xref.title: Wig Hairspray Catching Fire
xref.body: Gene Simmons, a member of KISS, experienced incidents where the hairspray on his wig would catch fire during performances. His roadie, Dave Matthews, was tasked with dousing him with a wet towel to put out the flames. "Sometimes he'd be called upon to douse Gene Simmons with a wet towel when the hairspray he used on his wig caught fire."
